name: jeroen blokland
zh_summary: @jsblokland: Mario Draghi, remembered for "whatever it takes," now says the bar is high for the ECB to step in to contain widening French bond spreads.
en_summary: @jsblokland: Mario Draghi, remembered for "whatever it takes," now says the bar is high for the ECB to step in to contain widening French bond spreads.
text:
The bar is high!

Former ECB President Mario Draghi will forever be remembered for three magical words: “Whatever it takes.”

At the height of the European debt crisis, those words helped save the euro.

Now, Draghi says the bar is high for the ECB to step in and contain the widening spread on French government bonds.

“There is nothing that says that these instruments cannot be used when a country is under Excessive Deficit Procedure. But certainly the bar is a little higher for that use.”

Meanwhile, France stands out in the IMF's latest World Economic Outlook as the only advanced economy facing a downward revision to its growth forecast.

Growth is expected to be a measly 0.4% this year, with a budget deficit exceeding 5% of GDP.

And elections approaching.

With that combination, I expect bond markets to keep testing the ECB's willingness to intervene by pushing French spreads even wider.

France has become the euro zone's weakest link.

Goodbye!

For analyst Q&A rounds: 

Q: Citi explicitly challenged TSMC on AI financing, HBM, CoWoS, lasers and the risk of overbuilding capacity 

A: $TSM assessed CSP capex, DC construction conditions, customer financial conditions, and supply of critical components. 

Management's conclusion is still that "demand exceeds supply". As well as that AI accelerator revenue growth could exceed its previous 50%+ CAGR projection through 2029.

This is a more meaningful statement since it addresses some concerns regarding recent selloff. 

Q: JPM asked if wafer supply could be tighter in 2027 than in 2026 (demand visibility)

A: Wei (Chairman/CEO) stated $TSM even sends staff to verify DC construction progress on site. And after assessing all the factors, TSMC believes gap between supply and demand remains substantial.  

It could not determine whether the extent of the gap given customers continues to increase demand. 

Q: On pricing power:

A: Wei responded that there is "no ceiling on TSMC's profitability" but that profits will not surge dramatically overnight.

(Source: NextApple, Taiwanese press)

- TSMC record profits of $23.6B (68% Y/Y growth), and revenue jumping to $46.72B, beating expectations.

- Q4 Guidance was $52.3-$54.3B revenue off 65-67% gross margins.

TLDR:

- No signs of any slowdown or collapse as AI demand far exceeds supply for fo

name: Steve Hanke
zh_summary: @steve_hanke: Japan's M2 grew 2.0% in September, well below his 6.1% golden growth rate for the BoJ's 2% target, so Japanese monetary policy is super tight.
en_summary: @steve_hanke: Japan's M2 grew 2.0% in September, well below his 6.1% golden growth rate for the BoJ's 2% target, so Japanese monetary policy is super tight.
text:
Japan’s money supply (M2) grew at 2.0%/yr in the month of September. That's well below Hanke’s Golden Growth Rate of 6.1%/yr, a rate consistent with the BoJ’s 2% inflation target.

Contrary to what most of the financial press says, monetary policy in Japan is SUPER TIGHT.

zh_summary: $TSM TSMC CFO expects 2026–2028 CapEx to significantly exceed the previous three years due to strong conviction in the AI megatrend. CapEx is a step up to support customers' growth, no intention to leave demand for others. Tool price inflation is real but majority of CapEx related to long-term demand. en_summary: $TSM TSMC CFO expects 2026–2028 CapEx to significantly exceed the previous three years due to strong conviction in the AI megatrend. CapEx is a step up to support customers' growth, no intention to leave demand for others. Tool price inflation is real but majority of CapEx related to long-term demand. If executed well, revenue increase will outpace CapEx increase.
text:
$TSM TSMC CFO expects 2026–2028 CapEx to significantly exceed the previous three years.

"We have very strong conviction in the AI megatrend. Therefore, our CapEx from 2026 to 2028 is expected to be significantly higher than the past 3 years. And this is a step up of our investment to support the customers' growth. We have no intention to leave any food on the table for others.

"The tool price inflation is real. The tool price, material, labor cost, et cetera. However, the majority of the CapEx is always related to the long-term demand. So that will be the composition going forward. And capital intensity-wise, as we always said, if do our job right, the increase in revenue will outpace the increase in CapEx, and that is still the case from what we are looking at."

text:
Ep 209 of Facts vs Feelings is here!

The bull market turned four this week 🎂

@sonusvarghese and I dig into what's driving it and where the stress is building

📈 The S&P 500 is up about 118% since October 2022, or 131% with dividends. Every bull market in the last 50 years that reached its third birthday went on to see a fifth.

💰 Profit growth accounts for roughly 85 points of the gain, about 40 of them from margin expansion. This year the forward P/E fell from about 22x to 19.5x as Treasury yields climbed, and earnings growth more than offset it.

💳 CCC spreads are near 900 bps. High yield overall is flat, and rate-hedged high yield and loans are beating cash. Ryan and Sonu see a duration problem from rising yields.

🏦 Hyperscaler bonds went from 1-2% of net new Treasury borrowing to about 14% in a year. SpaceX raised roughly $150B in four months, and its five-year CDS hit a record 200 bps.

🤖 Billions in AI compute contracts start billing between 2027 and 2029. Sonu flags 2027 and 2028 as the potential reckoning for the AI capex cycle.

We also cover small caps vs higher yields, the dollar back above 100 on the DXY, and next week's midterm episode with PIMCO's Libby Cantrell.

👇👇
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DK_wZ8ap1uA

name: Trung Phan
zh_summary: @TrungTPhan: Apple's market cap closed above $5 trillion for the first time, noting it suffered two 80% drawdowns (1991 to 1997 and 2000 to 2003).
en_summary: @TrungTPhan: Apple's market cap closed above $5 trillion for the first time, noting it suffered two 80% drawdowns (1991 to 1997 and 2000 to 2003).
text:
Apple market cap closed above $5 trillion for the first time today.

If you had invested in $1 in 1990, you would have $0 today because your paper hands would have definitely sold during one of its two 80% drawdowns (1991 to 1997 or 2000 to 2003).
